newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Collins to head Russia embassy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Collins to head Russia embassy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday nominated James Collins, a senior State Department adviser on the new states that emerged from the old Soviet Union, as the next U.S. ambassador to Russia.

Collins' nomination was long anticipated to fill the vacancy left in January in the Moscow embassy by Thomas Pickering, now undersecretary of state for political affairs. The nomination requires Senate confirmation.

Collins, a native of Aurora, Ill., currently serves as special adviser to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright for the new independent states of the old Soviet Union. He did a three-year tour as deputy chief of mission at the American Embassy in Moscow.
In a long diplomatic career, Collins has held a wide array of positions in the State Department. He also served in postings in Jordan and Turkey.
